concerns.text: T103 mandates statistical_report.json with 'top-level keys p_values and t_statistics (one entry per outcome)' and claims 'validity_status matching the output contract', but the output contract requires a flat per-comparison object with keys comparison_name, p_value, p_value_corrected, effect_size, effect_size_ci_lower/upper, significance_status, mdes, adjustment_status, validity_status. No task produces a contract-conformant statistical_report.json; an implementer following T103 verbatim cannot satisfy the contract.

No task covers schema-conformance to the dataset contract: the contract names the optional field 'mmse_score' (integer) while T102 maps/outputs 'MMSE' (float), and the data model names the condition field 'stimulus_condition' while all tasks use 'stimulus_type'. The plan's structure also lists tests/contract/ schema-validation tests, but no task creates them. Add a task (or amend T102) to reconcile field names/types and validate cleaned outputs against contracts/dataset.schema.yaml.

T110 writes hashes to 'state/state.yaml', but the constitution requires checksums in 'state/projects/PROJ-524-the-impact-of-nostalgia-on-cognitive-fle.yaml' under the artifact_hashes map. No task covers writing to the constitution-mandated state file, so Principle V/III versioning coverage is broken as written.

The plan's 'Methodological Simulation' synthetic-data fallback (a plan element) has no covering task — tasks.md removes it and mandates raising RealDataFetchFailed instead. The two artifacts prescribe opposite failure behavior; either the plan must be revised to remove the fallback or a task must implement the plan's labeled-simulation path. As written, an implementer cannot satisfy both.

The coverage map omits the plan's 'mixed-effects models if repeated measures are unexpectedly found' alternative (plan.md Critical Design Note) — no task detects or handles repeated measures. If intentionally dropped, state so; otherwise add a detection/handling step so the plan element is not silently uncovered.
